In the middle of Pokhara's Phewa Lake there is a temple you can only reach by boat. 🛶🙏

Tal Barahi is a small two-storey pagoda on an island in the lake, dedicated to the goddess Barahi, the boar form of the mother goddess Ajima, worshipped by many as a form of Durga.

🛶 Wooden boats carry devotees across from the Lakeside shore
🪔 It is at its busiest during the fairs of Baisakh and Kartik
🏔️ On a clear morning, Machhapuchare rises above the hills behind the lake

A boat ride on Phewa Lake is included on our 7-day Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan tour, private to your family, with a guide and a private vehicle the whole way.

Have you ever prayed somewhere you had to row to? 👇

Most Himalayan treks start with a flight. This one starts with a drive. 🏔️

The Langtang Valley is the closest major trekking region to Kathmandu, about 7–8 hours by road to the trailhead at Syabrubesi.

Our 10-day Langtang Valley Trek:
🚙 Day 2 — private drive to Syabrubesi (1,460 m)
🌲 Days 3–4 — through the forest to Lama Hotel and Langtang Village (3,430 m)
🛕 Day 5 — Kyanjin Gompa (3,870 m)
⛰️ Day 6 — optional climb of Kyanjin Ri (4,773 m) or Tserko Ri (4,984 m)

Langtang National Park permit and TIMS card, teahouse lodges, breakfast and dinner on the trek, a licensed guide and porter support are included. Private to your group.

Would you rather drive to the mountains or fly? 👇

A walled city on a high desert, north of the Annapurnas. 🏜️

Upper Mustang was a closed kingdom until 1992, and you still need a special restricted area permit and a licensed guide to walk in.

Our 16-day Upper Mustang Trek:
✈️ Day 3 — fly Pokhara to Jomsom, walk to Kagbeni (2,800 m)
🏘️ Days 4–7 — Chele, Syanbochen, Ghami and Tsarang
⛰️ Day 8 — over the Lo La pass (3,950 m) to Lo Manthang
🏯 Day 9 — a full day in Lo Manthang, the 15th-century walled capital of the former Kingdom of Mustang

The Restricted Area Permit and ACAP, the flights, teahouse and guesthouse stays, breakfast and dinner on the trek, a licensed guide and porter support are included. Private to your group.

More than 2,200 years ago, an emperor travelled to a garden in southern Nepal to pray. 🙏

In 249 BC, Emperor Ashoka came to Lumbini and raised a stone pillar. Its inscription records that he came himself to worship, because the Buddha Shakyamuni was born here.

🪷 Inside the Maya Devi Temple, a marker stone marks the spot where the Buddha was born
💧 Beside the temple is the sacred pond where Maya Devi is believed to have bathed before his birth
🛕 Around them, the Monastic Zone holds monasteries built by Buddhist nations from around the world

Today Lumbini is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, open to people of every faith.

Our 7-day Lumbini & Pokhara tour brings you to Lumbini on Day 5 for sightseeing with a guide, entry fees included, private to your family.
